correctness.rationale: A base-B diagonal cocharacter with B>d gives distinct weights to all degree-d monomials, so every fixed point is a monomial coordinate point. For a two-variable monomial with smaller exponent b, the degree-b catalecticant has rank b+1; explicit finite-difference degenerations attain border rank at most two for b=1 and at most three for b=2. Support at least four gives first-catalecticant rank at least four. Three-variable support with d>=4 gives quadratic-catalecticant rank at least four. For d=3, the only three-support monomial has nonzero Aronhold invariant using Han's displayed quartic, excluding it from sigma_3. The resulting monomial counts are m^2, m^2+C(m,2), and m(2m-1), and projective C*-localization converts them to Euler characteristics. Subtracting the independently reconstructed rank-at-most-two fixed count m^2 gives the exact-layer formulas. The packaged checker enumerates monomials, catalecticant divisor counts, and separated weights on a finite grid as regression evidence.

originality.rationale: Three highly relevant archival sources were inspected at statement level. Landsberg--Ottaviani develop the exact Veronese secant equations and catalecticants, Buczynski--Landsberg classify border-rank-three normal forms, and Han treats exactly sigma_3(v_d(P^n)) including the cubic Aronhold case; none of the inspected texts gives an Euler or Poincare formula. Targeted semantic-index searches and exact web searches for third Veronese secants with Euler characteristic, topology, Poincare polynomial, torus fixed points, and symmetric border-rank-three strata did not locate a covering result. The prior rank-two Euler theorem implies only the baseline m^2 and does not determine which new fixed monomials enter sigma_3. The accepted claim is therefore the third-secant trichotomy itself, not the already-covered rank-two special case.

value.rationale: Third Veronese secants are a classical and heavily studied low-border-rank family with dedicated literature on equations, normal forms, singularities, and identifiability. The theorem gives a uniform global invariant in every ambient dimension and reveals a nontrivial three-regime transition in the polynomial degree. The exact third layer has zero Euler mass for cubics, one unordered-pair contribution for quartics, and one ordered-pair contribution from degree five onward, directly exposing which new border-rank-three monomial orbit types appear. This is a structural classification-driven invariant of the full family rather than an arbitrary parameter slice or a numerical recomputation.
